source: Minchat Shai on Gen 12:8 (citing the Masorah; Bereshit Rabbah 39:23)
claim_en: aholoh ('his tent') written with final HEH (as if 'her tent') — one of FOUR so written; the midrash: he pitched Sarah's tent first. Torah census: exactly four heh-written tokens (9:21 Noah's, 12:8, 13:3, 35:21).

ha-nireh ('who APPEARED') — two in the Masorah: here and at Jacob's return to Beit El (35:1), 'as He appeared to Abraham when he wandered, so to Jacob when he wandered.' Both tokens are Torah-side: exactly two.
areka ('I will show you') — the Masorah pairs it with one other in Zechariah (the exiles shown to Abraham). Torah-side: exactly ONE token (12:1); the Zechariah leg rides as an inheritance edge.

va-avarakhah ('and I will bless') — the Masorah pairs it with 'I will bless Your name forever' (Ps 145:1): 'a blessing that never stops.' Torah-side: exactly ONE token (12:3); the Psalms leg rides as an inheritance edge.

mevarakhekha ('those who bless you' — PLURAL, against the singular belittler) — whole Torah career: exactly TWO tokens, 12:3 and Num 24:9, Balaam's mouth ('blessed are those who bless you'). The Kitzur's own arithmetic on the curse-half points at Balaam; the census delivers Balaam as the word's only other holder.
mevarakhekha 'must be written with YOD' (the plural marker) — both Torah tokens carry the yod plene.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 12:3 (manuscript Masorah he quotes)
claim_en: The bless-word vocalization law, arm 2: accent on the KAF — the resh takes sheva+patach (the compound half-vowel). va-avarakhah's accent sits on the kaf-syllable; SNAPSHOT's resh carries hataf patach.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 12:3 (manuscript Masorah he quotes)
claim_en: The same law at the word's OTHER Torah token: Balaam's mevarakhekha carries its accent on the kaf — and SNAPSHOT's resh there carries hataf patach. The two tokens of the one word split exactly along the quoted accent-law.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 12:3 (his own ruling line)
claim_en: 'I walk in the way of the books, which are all with simple sheva alone; the precise reader who pronounces properly — blessing upon him.' SNAPSHOT (12:3) writes the resh of mevarakhekha with SIMPLE SHEVA — the way of the books, exactly his bottom line.
'galgal (the wheel-sign) on the BET' of mevarakhekha — SNAPSHOT carries a sign at exactly that position, encoded as munach: the wheel-sign variant class again (4th recurrence).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 12:8 (Masekhet Soferim; Yerushalmi Megillah)
claim_en: Beit El — among the names written as TWO WORDS (the lists dispute whether it divides; the old manuscript: never split across two lines). SNAPSHOT: two word-rows JOINED BY MAQQEF — first occurrence (le-veit El).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 12:8 (Masekhet Soferim; Yerushalmi Megillah)
claim_en: Beit El, second occurrence in the verse — again two written words joined by maqqef: divided in writing, one in breath.
va-yiven ('and he built'), the SECOND build-verb: 'without qadma.' SNAPSHOT agrees — meteg only (probe: no qadma sign anywhere on the token; the first build-verb at 12:7 carries mahpakh).

DISCREPANCY OBSERVATION — mizbeach ('altar', 12:8): Minchat Shai rules 'the LAST pashta ALONE' (Sephardic codices double pashta only when a letter separates the two). SNAPSHOT (Leningrad line) writes BOTH signs — the medial qadma-position sign plus the final pashta. Tradition vs SNAPSHOT, accent-writing convention: filed, not merged.
lekh-lekha ('go, you') opens a PETUCHA (open paragraph) — paragraph-break class: the instrument cannot see paragraph layout.

THREE TAGIN (letter-crowns) on the final kaf of va-avarekhekha ('and I will bless you') — three twenties = sixty, against the sixty letters of the priestly blessing. Letter-CROWN layer: a NEW member of the uninstrumented family.
